name: Pipe joint beveling, tacking and circumferential weld

steps.title: Safety gear and welding PPE inspection
steps.visual_criteria: Auto-darkening welding helmet, leather gloves, flame-resistant jacket, and safety boots properly worn

steps.title: Metal pipe preparation and edge beveling
steps.visual_criteria: Pipe ends cleaned of rust, paint, and oil using wire brush; uniform 30-35 degree bevel angle created

steps.title: Pipe alignment and bridge tack welding
steps.visual_criteria: Root gap set to 2-3mm with spacer; 3 to 4 uniform bridge tack welds placed at 90-degree intervals

steps.title: Full circumferential pass weld execution
steps.visual_criteria: Smooth, continuous root and fill pass with uniform bead width, proper penetration, and no burn-through

steps.title: Slag removal and joint inspection
steps.visual_criteria: Slag completely chipped off with chipping hammer and wire-brushed clean; no visible porosity or undercut

scenario_questions.text: What essential personal protective equipment must be verified before striking an electric arc?
expected_points: Welding helmet with correct shade lens and safety glasses underneath
Dry leather welding gloves and fire-resistant leather apron or jacket

scenario_questions.text: Why is thorough slag removal and cleaning required between successive weld passes?
expected_points: Prevents slag inclusions and internal porosity in the weld deposit
Ensures complete fusion between successive passes

scenario_questions.text: What fire prevention checks must be conducted in the immediate welding area before commencing work?
expected_points: Remove all flammable and combustible materials within at least 10 meters
Keep a certified fire extinguisher within immediate reach
Ensure adequate ventilation or fume extraction

common_mistakes: Welding without proper eye and skin UV protection
Inadequate root opening causing lack of root penetration
Failing to clean slag before the subsequent weld pass causing inclusions
Incorrect arc length causing excessive spatter and undercut
